title: YOU Are the Hero - Damn Right I Am!
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b4fNiXZPqRQ

Daniel (@dungeondive) flips through Jonathan Green's *YOU Are the Hero*, a revised, Kickstarted history of the Fighting Fantasy gamebooks — and the book becomes a doorway into his own childhood. He recalls the early-80s spell those books cast, the well-loved copies read until their spines gave way, and the handful he still owns (*The Warlock of Firetop Mountain*, *The Citadel of Chaos*, *Scorpion Swamp*) in their US editions. He lingers on Steve Jackson's *Sorcery!* series and its John Blanche interior art, the memorise-your-spells rule he never actually followed, and *Advanced Fighting Fantasy*'s *Dungeoneer*. Green's book earns his highest praise for doing what Games Workshop's own *Illustrated Guide* failed to do: crediting every artist — Ian McCaig, Russ Nicholson, John Blanche — and celebrating the covers that shaped a generation. Along the way he tells the story of writing to the US publisher over a printing error and receiving a handwritten reply inside a box of free gamebooks, "one of my most cherished memories." A nostalgic, heartfelt recommendation.

----

What was your gateway gamebook — and did any of your copies survive in one piece, or read themselves to bits?
